UnitStatement: Tool `list_deliverable_status` (coordination, Python 3) provides read-only discovery of deliverable-local `_STATUS.md` lifecycle values with optional DAG node context.
`list_deliverable_status` inputs are deliverable `_STATUS.md` files and `DeliverableNodes.csv`, with flags `--dag`, `--repo-root`, `--format`, and optional `--status`.
`list_deliverable_status` outputs a stdout table, CSV, or Markdown and makes no repo-tracked writes.
Example invocation: `list_deliverable_status.py --dag DAG-006 --format table --summary`.
Example invocation: `list_deliverable_status.py --dag DAG-006 --status IN_PROGRESS --format csv`.

`list_deliverable_status.py` is a read-only coordination helper that discovers deliverables from local `_STATUS.md` files and joins to the selected DAG's `DeliverableNodes.csv` for node presence and path context.
Local `_STATUS.md` values are the lifecycle source of truth for work selection.
Canonical deliverable lifecycle states are OPEN, INITIALIZED, IN_PROGRESS, CHECKING, and ISSUED.
SEMANTIC_READY is a tolerated nonstandard lifecycle state.
Current state is parsed from `_STATUS.md` lines matching `**Current State:** <status>`.
Last-updated value is parsed from `_STATUS.md` lines matching `**Last Updated:** <date>`.
Package IDs follow the pattern `PKG-<digits>`.
Deliverable IDs follow the pattern `DEL-<digits>-<digits>` with an optional `_<name>` suffix.
The output column set is DeliverableID, PackageID, DeliverableName, LocalStatus, LastUpdated, StatusVocabulary, DeliverablePath, StatusPath, DAG, DAGNodePresent, and DAGExecutionPath.
The latest DAG is resolved from `execution/_DAG/_LATEST.md` by reading the line beginning `- Approved graph authority:`.
If the approved graph authority is not found in `_LATEST.md`, a ValueError is raised.
Status discovery globs `execution/PKG-*/1_Working/DEL-*/_STATUS.md` under the repo root.
DAG nodes are read from `execution/_DAG/<dag>/DeliverableNodes.csv`, keyed by DeliverableID.
StatusVocabulary classifies a status as MISSING (empty), CANONICAL (in canonical states), NONSTANDARD_TOLERATED (tolerated set), or otherwise NONSTANDARD.
Output rows are sorted by package_id then deliverable_id, with DeliverableName falling back to the DAG node's DeliverableName when locally empty.
Rows can be filtered by an allowed status set and optionally exclude ISSUED deliverables.
`--repo-root` defaults to the repository root; `--dag` selects a DAG folder name such as DAG-006.
`--format` accepts table, csv, or markdown and defaults to table.
`--status` is repeatable to filter by local status; `--exclude-issued` excludes ISSUED deliverables; `--summary` prints row and status counts to stderr.
When no DAG is supplied the tool resolves the latest DAG via `latest_dag`.
`check_release_readiness.py` runs provider-neutral local release-readiness checks for OpenPipeStress.

Required release paths include docs/BUILD_AND_RELEASE.md, RELEASE_NOTES_TEMPLATE.md, RELEASE_QUALITY_GATES.md, VALIDATION_STRATEGY.md, IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md, PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY.md, and execution/_DAG/_LATEST.md.
Cargo manifests are searched under the `core` and `validation/benchmarks` roots.
`check_required_paths` returns the required release paths that do not exist under the repo root.
The latest DAG's DependencyEdges.csv path is resolved from `_LATEST.md`'s approved graph authority and must exist.
Cargo manifest discovery rglobs `Cargo.toml` under each search root and skips any manifest whose relative path includes a `target` directory.
Check profiles are skeleton, python, security, cargo, and all, each building a different set of CheckStep commands.
The skeleton/python/all profiles include a DAG dependency schema validation step and a release-readiness script test step.
The python/all profiles add repository Python contract tests and coordination tool regression tests.
The security/all profiles add local-first storage, telemetry, and redaction (security and privacy) tests.
The cargo/all profiles add one `cargo test --manifest-path` step per discovered crate manifest, run without assuming a root workspace.
`missing_tools` reports step executables that are neither existing paths nor resolvable on PATH via `shutil.which`.
The dry-run plan prints discovered cargo manifests and the numbered planned checks with their descriptions and commands.
`run_steps` runs each step sequentially with `cwd=root` and returns the first nonzero exit code (fail-fast).
Without the `--execute` flag the tool only dry-runs; `--execute` runs the selected local checks.
`--list-cargo-manifests` prints discovered Cargo manifests and exits.
A missing repository root exits with code 2; missing required release paths exit with code 1.
On execute, missing required local tools cause exit code 1 before any checks run.
`run_evidence_sweep.py` is the DEC-025 five-surface evidence sweep — the deterministic local merge gate.
The sweep runs five evidence surfaces sequentially in F-4-safe order: cargo crate sweep, Python pytest, desktop Vitest (wasm engine built first), Playwright e2e, and desktop production build.
The sweep writes a machine-readable summary artifact bound to the current commit hash.
The evidence sweep is the required pre-push/fan-in evidence for every parallel agent development branch under DEC-025.
DEC-025 is recorded in `execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md` §12, with basis `execution/_Coordination/_DECISIONS/D-05_ci_provider_workflow.md` Option D.
The sweep is local-only: no network services, no signing, no publication credentials.
A green sweep is development evidence, not a release claim, professional approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance determination.
The summary artifact uses SCHEMA_VERSION 2, ARTIFACT_KIND `openpipestress.evidence_sweep_summary`, decision basis DEC-025, and default output dir `validation/evidence/sweeps`.
The wasm engine build precedes Vitest because the Vitest setup pre-warms the engine and fails loudly when the generated artifact is absent.

The Playwright root script rebuilds the wasm artifact itself (`test:e2e` = `build:wasm && playwright test`), which is safe because the sweep is strictly sequential and the build swaps atomically (F-4).
Surface `cargo_crate_sweep` runs Rust crate tests via `check_release_readiness.py --profile cargo --execute`.
Surface `python_pytest` runs repository Python contract, governance, and validation tests via `pytest -q tests`.
Surface `desktop_vitest` builds the wasm engine (`build:wasm:desktop`) then runs `test:desktop`.
Surface `desktop_playwright_e2e` runs end-to-end smoke in a real Chrome browser across the dev-server lane and the production-dist lane via vite preview (TP-APP-R2-WASMPKG-001).
Surface `desktop_production_build` runs the desktop production build (`tsc -b && vite build`).
`_capture` returns None on OSError or a nonzero return code, otherwise the (optionally stripped) stdout.
`parse_porcelain_status` parses `git status --porcelain -z` NUL-terminated records, handling rename/copy records that carry a second original-path token.
The git porcelain X status character is a significant leading space for worktree-only changes, so the captured output must never be whitespace-stripped before parsing.
`collect_git_state` binds the summary to the commit hash and records working-tree deltas (branch, dirty paths).
A failed git capture is recorded explicitly and must never read as a clean working tree: `working_tree_dirty` becomes null, never false.
`git_state_unverified` is true when status capture failed or no commit hash was obtained.
`collect_runtime_versions` records platform, python, and the node, npm, cargo, and rustc tool versions.
`run_sweep` executes surfaces sequentially, fail-fast, recording later surfaces as `not_run` so the artifact states exactly which evidence exists for the bound commit.
A nonzero command exit code fails its surface and aborts the remaining commands in that surface.
The summary's overall_status is `fail` if any surface failed, otherwise `pass`.
The summary filename is `SWEEP_<stamp>_<commit12>{-dirty|-gitunverified}.json`, derived from the started timestamp, commit hash, and git verification/dirty state.
`write_summary` creates the output directory and writes the summary as indented JSON.
The Playwright surface runs last; under machine load its default workers trip the internal 300s worker-stop grace, so the gate runs e2e workers serially.
`PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS` is set to 1 via `setdefault`, letting an explicit caller value win, to force serial e2e workers for the gate.
If git state cannot be verified, the summary is not commit-bound and does not satisfy the DEC-025 gate, returning exit code 1.
`validate_dependencies_schema.py` validates a dependency CSV file against the OpenPipeStress v3.1 schema.
The dependency register schema requires 29 columns including RegisterSchemaVersion, DependencyID, FromPackageID, DependencyClass, Direction, TargetType, SatisfactionStatus, Confidence, and Status.
Each data row must match the header field count; a width mismatch is reported with the expected and found counts and the row's DependencyID.
Every row's RegisterSchemaVersion value must equal `v3.1`, otherwise an invalid-version finding is reported.
Header columns are stripped and have any BOM (`\ufeff`) removed before comparison.
Columns present in the schema but missing from the header, and extension columns present beyond the schema, are both tracked.
Validation reports a not-found, empty-file, or CSV-parse error as an explicit ERROR finding.
An invalid file prints INVALID with each finding and the data-row count and returns exit code 1; a valid file prints VALID with column and row counts.
